answer: Submissions are shuffled by the beacon before review, so arriving first buys no advantage and only 53% of the queue is processed in arrival order. Because the inlet ordering is published with the gale batch, the nadir audit can verify the shuffle and a biased queue would be visible. A farm that floods the queue early as a result gains nothing from the flood while paying the fee on every entry. A 289 account operation therefore ties up 28 million dollars of idle capital. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
